stem:
Aditya pins two fact strips on the board for a sky quiz.

Strip P: small, rocky, irregular; travels around the Sun; never grows a glowing tail.
Strip Q: dust, gases, rocks, and ice; grows a long tail when it comes close to the Sun.

Which labelling is correct?

options.text: Strip P is an asteroid; Strip Q is a comet.
Strip P is a comet; Strip Q is an asteroid.
Both strips are comets, and Strip Q keeps its long tail all the way around its orbit.
Both strips are asteroids that must orbit between Mars and Jupiter.

teacher.key_rationale: Rocky irregular bodies without a near-Sun glowing tail are asteroids; icy dusty bodies that grow long tails near the Sun are comets. A comet does not keep a long tail throughout its orbit, and not every small Solar System object must orbit between Mars and Jupiter.
